title: Power Apps: Power Platform connectors in generative pages

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing promises data-policy enforcement for generative pages without supporting documentation and incorrectly applies Managed Environments sharing limits to model-driven apps. The admin opt-in default, licensing classification and connection-reference controls also need correction before administrators can rely on the page.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Makers can bring Power Platform connector data into generative pages.
claims.quote: Connector support lets a generative page use data outside of Dataverse through the Power Platform connector ecosystem.

claims.claim: Using connector data requires creating and authenticating a connection.
claims.quote: If your page uses a Power Platform connector (preview), create and authenticate a connection.

claims.claim: The page uses a connection reference in the environment.
claims.quote: Then open Solutions > Default Solution and create a connection reference that uses the connection.

claims.claim: The maker selects connector data and describes how the page should use it.
claims.quote: select the prepared connection reference, and choose the connector data that the page should use. In your prompt, describe how you want the page to use the selected data.

claims.claim: Connector data can be incorporated through either the generative page designer or the generative pages AI plugin.
claims.quote: Connector data can be incorporated while working in the Maker Studio generative page designer or through the generative pages AI plugin.

claims.claim: GitHub Copilot CLI is one of the tools supported for the plugin-based authoring experience.
claims.quote: This article describes how to use AI code generation tools, such as GitHub Copilot CLI, to create and edit generative pages for model-driven apps in Power Apps.

claims.claim: The in-browser designer exposes connector data under Add data > Connectors.
claims.quote: To use data from a Power Platform connector (preview), select Add data > Connectors, select the prepared connection reference, and choose the connector data that the page should use.

claims.claim: Learn currently labels connector support in generative pages as preview.
claims.quote: Connector support, Custom API support, and Application Insights telemetry for generative pages are preview features.

claims.where: Why it matters: Generated pages stop being limited to Dataverse tables
claims.claim: Before this change, generative pages were limited to Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "previously" "Dataverse". Opened generative-pages and generative-page-external-tools; their current data-source descriptions do not establish this historical restriction.
claims.fix: Replace the historical claim with 'Connector support lets generative pages use data outside Dataverse.'

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: A generative page can read or change external data through connectors, including SharePoint, SQL and SaaS services.
claims.quote:
| `createConnectorRow` | Creates a new row in the specified connector table. |
| `updateConnectorRow` | Updates an existing row in the specified connector table. |
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/generative-page/data-api/connector-methods to sources for read/write operations. The already-cited external-tools page states that all Power Platform connectors are supported in preview.

claims.where: Why it matters: Because code is AI-generated
claims.claim: Generative pages contain AI-generated code.
claims.quote: the system then processes your requirements and specifications and intelligently generates React code

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Connector-backed pages can show connector data to app users.
claims.quote: For example, ask the agent to create a page that displays documents from a SharePoint list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing the connector plan before build approval and testing with users' identities and permissions.
claims.quote: Review the connector data source in the plan before you approve the build. Test the generated page with the identities and permissions that your users will use.

claims.claim: Connections carry authentication credentials.
claims.quote: A connection is a stored authentication credential for a connector, for example OAuth credentials for the SharePoint connector.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-connection-reference to sources.

claims.claim: Generated page code can write data through connector operations.
claims.quote:
| `createConnectorRow` | Creates a new row in the specified connector table. |
| `deleteConnectorRow` | Deletes a row from the specified connector table. |
claims.fix: Cite the connector-methods reference for the supported write operations; retain the advice to review the plan.

claims.claim: Broken or expired connections will produce user-facing errors.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "connector" "expired". Opened external-tools and connector-methods. The API documents rejected promises and error results, not guaranteed user-facing errors for expired connections.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Connection failures can interrupt page operations; review generated error handling and test failed or unauthorised connections.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/generative-page/data-api/connector-methods.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first sentence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Separate licensing terms specific to connector support in generative pages have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "licensing"; "generative pages" "connector" "licensing" "credits". Opened generative-pages, external-tools and Power Apps licensing FAQs: general licensing and maker-credit guidance, but no separate connector-feature terms.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Existing Power Apps licensing requires appropriate premium entitlements for premium connectors.
claims.quote: Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors, Dataverse entities, on-premises data gateways, custom APIs, etc.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-licensing-faq. Clarify that model-driven apps already require premium use rights, so adding a premium connector does not by itself establish an incremental licence purchase.

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is per-user.
claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally, use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'unknown' if it describes this feature's unpublished separate terms. Explain the general Power Apps entitlement options in notes, rather than assigning a single per-user model; cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-licensing-faq.

claims.claim: This change has a known medium direct cost because premium connectors may require additional user licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: generative pages connectors licensing premium connectors Power Apps license meter. Opened generative-pages and Power Apps licensing FAQs: model-driven apps already require premium rights; no incremental connector-feature licence or charge is stated.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'low' for the evidenced review and pilot work, and state that any separate feature-specific licensing is not yet published. Do not infer new licence purchases from premium connectors in an already-premium model-driven app.

claims.claim: Nobody can use connector support in generative pages until an administrator opts in.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "enable" "admin"; "generative pages" "connector" "PowerShell" "disable". Opened generative-pages and external-tools prerequisites: maker-selected connector use is described, but no required administrator enablement.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in': the documented maker workflow selects connector data, and the targeted searches found no feature-specific admin switch. Do not classify creation of a connection reference as administrator opt-in.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy opens data-policy creation.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Security, and then on the Security pane, select Data and privacy.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy belongs to Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell and creates a data policy.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the `NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition` object.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering is configured through Data policy > Prebuilt Connectors > Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.quote: If the value of the Endpoint configurable column is Yes, you can use this capability by right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.fix: Expand the path to select or edit a data policy, then Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints. Say this is preview and only applies where Endpoint configurable is Yes. Remove custom connectors from the row's scope.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations creates connector configurations containing endpoint filtering rules.
claims.quote:
Create connector configurations for a data policy

New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations
claims.fix: Flag endpoint filtering as preview and restrict the row to supported prebuilt connectors. The command exists, but neither this command nor this reference establishes custom-connector endpoint filtering.

claims.claim: Solutions > Default Solution > connection reference is the documented path for setting up the connection reference.
claims.quote: On the command bar, select New > More > Connection Reference.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Solutions > Default Solution > New > More > Connection Reference'. Retain the feature prerequisite link and add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-connection-reference for the creation steps.

claims.claim: No API or automation surface is documented for managing the connection reference.
claims.quote:
Entity set path:
[organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/connectionreferences
Operations supported:
POSTGETPATCHDELETE
claims.fix: Replace api:null with a Dataverse REST control, for example 'GET [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/connectionreferences', citing this entity reference; explain that POST and PATCH create and update references. Do not label connection-reference automation undocumented.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth row
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no environment switch specific to connector support in generative pages, in either UI or automation.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "enable" "admin"; "generative pages" "connector" "PowerShell" "disable". Opened generative-pages and external-tools; reviewed pac model search excerpts. No feature-specific enable/disable control was documented.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph after table; controls[0] and controls[1]; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Data policies govern generative pages exactly as they govern canvas apps and flows.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "data policies"; "generative pages" "DLP". Opened generative-pages, external-tools, connector-action-control and connector-endpoint-filtering. None states equivalent data-policy enforcement for generative pages.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion of equivalent enforcement. Label the data-policy and endpoint-filtering rows as general platform controls whose applicability to generative pages Microsoft has not confirmed in the sources checked, and repeat this uncertainty in Open questions.

claims.where: Governance controls: a blocked connector cannot be referenced
claims.claim: A data-policy-blocked connector cannot be referenced by a generative page.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "data policies"; "generative pages" "DLP". Read generative-pages, external-tools and the cited connector control references; no passage establishes blocking of generative-page connection references.
claims.fix: Remove 'a blocked connector cannot be referenced'. Replace it with an open question about how data-policy blocking is enforced for designer-created and plugin-created generative pages.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls: endpoint row scope
claims.claim: The cited endpoint-filtering control filters endpoints for HTTP and custom connectors.
claims.quote:
it's exclusively available for the following connectors:
- HTTP
- HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (AD)
- HTTP Webhook
- SQL Server
claims.fix: Remove 'custom connectors' from the endpoint-filtering row; the exclusive supported list does not include them. Describe this preview control as endpoint filtering for supported prebuilt connectors.

claims.where: Governance controls: Connection references are maker-managed
claims.claim: Makers can manage the connection references used by generative pages.
claims.quote: Then open Solutions > Default Solution and create a connection reference that uses the connection.

claims.where: Governance controls: connection references travel with the solution
claims.claim: Connection references are solution components that can move with a solution.
claims.quote: A connection reference is a solution component that contains a reference to a connection about a specific connector.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-connection-reference and clarify that the target environment supplies the connection during solution import; credentials are not implied to travel with the solution.

claims.where: Governance controls: Managed Environments sharing limits
claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing limits apply to the model-driven app carrying a generative page.
claims.quote: In managed environments, admins can limit how broadly users can share canvas apps, flows, and agents.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that Managed Environments sharing limits govern the host model-driven app. The documented sharing-limit controls cover canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agents, not model-driven apps.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to define who may create connection references, but the controls table does not identify a creation-permission control.
claims.quote:
Define who may create connection references in each environment.
Connection reference the page uses
claims.fix: Add a separate row for permission to create connection references, with verified control surfaces, or replace the checklist instruction with an ownership review that the existing connection-reference row actually covers.

claims.claim: Connector action control on a data policy can narrow the individual actions exposed by a permitted connector.
claims.quote: You can use connector action control to allow or block individual actions or triggers within a given connector.
